article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "If you were asked to identify Johannes Vermeer , you might answer that he is one of the world’s most famous Old Masters, that his Girl with the Pearl Earring (ca. 1665) is perhaps the pinnacle of the Dutch Golden Age, or that he was one of the Netherlands’s greatest-ever artists."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But if you were to ask the same question to someone in 1800, the answer would likely be “who?”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "While his mammoth reputation today would suggest otherwise, for the 200 years following his death, Vermeer was largely forgotten. His unlikely return to the spotlight was thanks to a single French art critic. But why did he disappear?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "When Vermeer died aged just 43 in 1675, he was in debt and had mostly fallen into obscurity outside of his hometown of Delft in the Dutch Republic. Only 34 paintings are firmly accepted to have been painted by Vermeer, as he worked slowly and fastidiously. He didn’t work in a large studio, leaving no pupils behind who were dedicated to the continuation of his style after his death. He rarely travelled, and so had not built a reputation in major cities. His widow was forced to sell most of his works to pay off their debts, spreading his work across the country. All of these factors stunted the development of Vermeer’s legacy.", "links": [{"text": "into obscurity", "url": "https://www.vermeerdelft.nl/en/blogs/why-was-johannes-vermeer-not-well-known-during-his-lifetime"}, {"text": "hometown of Delft", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/art-world/vermeer-exhibition-amsterdam-delft-2254119"}, {"text": "Only 34 paintings", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/art-world/vermeer-paintings-ranked-1071242"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "By the mid-19th century, Vermeer was of such little repute that works by him were sometimes forged with a signature by Pieter de Hooch —an artist whose name carried significantly more weight at the time—to increase their prices. So how did he re-enter the spotlight?", "links": [{"text": "forged with a signature by Pieter de Hooch", "url": "https://artsandculture.google.com/story/rediscovering-vermeer-mauritshuis/CwWBo-zBwKmiLw?hl=en"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/app/news-upload/2026/08/GettyImages-2198973815-1024x853.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Artnet News"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Johannes Vermeer, View of Delft (ca. 1660–61). Photo: Buyenlarge/Getty Images."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Etienne-Joseph-Théophile Thoré was a French art critic and collector living in exile across Western Europe from 1849–1859 due to his support of French Revolutionary radicals. article_text:
If you were asked to identify Johannes Vermeer , you might answer that he is one of the world’s most famous Old Masters, that his Girl with the Pearl Earring (ca. 1665) is perhaps the pinnacle of the Dutch Golden Age, or that he was one of the Netherlands’s greatest-ever artists.

But if you were to ask the same question to someone in 1800, the answer would likely be “who?”

While his mammoth reputation today would suggest otherwise, for the 200 years following his death, Vermeer was largely forgotten. His unlikely return to the spotlight was thanks to a single French art critic. But why did he disappear?

When Vermeer died aged just 43 in 1675, he was in debt and had mostly fallen into obscurity outside of his hometown of Delft in the Dutch Republic. Only 34 paintings are firmly accepted to have been painted by Vermeer, as he worked slowly and fastidiously. He didn’t work in a large studio, leaving no pupils behind who were dedicated to the continuation of his style after his death. He rarely travelled, and so had not built a reputation in major cities. His widow was forced to sell most of his works to pay off their debts, spreading his work across the country. All of these factors stunted the development of Vermeer’s legacy.

By the mid-19th century, Vermeer was of such little repute that works by him were sometimes forged with a signature by Pieter de Hooch —an artist whose name carried significantly more weight at the time—to increase their prices. So how did he re-enter the spotlight?

Johannes Vermeer, View of Delft (ca. 1660–61). Photo: Buyenlarge/Getty Images.

Etienne-Joseph-Théophile Thoré was a French art critic and collector living in exile across Western Europe from 1849–1859 due to his support of French Revolutionary radicals. During that time, he wrote under the pseudonym W. Bürger . He had first seen Vermeer’s work, View of Delft (ca. 1660–61) in 1842 and was bowled over, but found locating more work by Vermeer so impossible that he referred to the artist as his “sphinx,” the riddle-providing creature of Greek mythology. As he travelled through Europe he began to collect paintings he believed could have been by the enigmatic artist.

In 1866, an exhibition of Old Master paintings was held at the Palais des Champs-Élysées and Thoré-Bürger contributed six Vermeer works to the show. Five additional paintings attributed to Vermeer were also displayed, although several were later reattributed to Vermeer’s contemporaries. Nonetheless, thanks to the exhibition and two articles Thoré-Bürger published about the artist, in addition to a catalogue of his works, Vermeer was back in the art world.

Johannes Vermeer, Girl with a Pearl Earring (ca. 1665). Photo: Sepia Times/ Universal Images Group via Getty Images.

The market took its time to catch up with Vermeer’s mounting legacy, however, and when Girl with a Pearl Earring came to auction in 1881 it sold for just two guilders and 30 cents—the equivalent of $35 . Today, estimates for the painting’s value reach $600 million.

After his death, a number of Thoré-Bürger’s Vermeer paintings were sold. Three of them are now held in public collections: A Young Woman Standing at a Virginal (ca. 1670–72) and A Young Woman Seated at the Virginal (ca. 1670–72) are at London’s National Gallery ; and Young Woman with a Pearl Necklace (ca. 1664) is held at Berlin’s Gemäldegalerie . Meanwhile, The Concert (1664), one of 13 works stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in 1990, is considered the most valuable missing piece of art in the world, valued at $200 million.

Another painting— A Young Woman Seated at the Virginals , long in a private Belgian collection—resurfaced at Sotheby’s London in 2004, selling for $30.1 million to casino magnate Steve Wynn . It was the first Vermeer to appear at public auction in over 80 years and remains his auction record.

Despite there being fewer than 40 known paintings attributed to him, thanks to Thoré-Bürger’s dogged pursuit of his sphinx, Vermeer isn’t going anywhere.

Sotheby’s Institute has been at the forefront of educating arts professionals for fifty years. The Institute now has more than 8,000 alumni around the globe who hold top positions in all facets of the international art world. To learn more about our programs in London, New York, and Online, visit www.sothebysinstitute.com .

article_text:
写真家・篠田優の個展「Garden」が、2026年9月18日から30日まで、東京・高田馬場のAlt_Mediumで開催される。本展で篠田が向き合うのは、親交のあった写真家・飯田鉄（1948–2023）が遺したフィルムと、その記憶だ。

展示される作品は、すべてモノクロームのフィルムで撮影されたもの。そのフィルム自体が、生前の飯田から篠田へと譲られたものだという。篠田はそれを用いて、飯田が撮影地として愛着を持っていた場所の風景と、飯田が自身の蔵書として集め、のちに篠田が受け継いだ書籍を撮影した。

写されるのは、すでに本人が不在となった場所と物。しかし、撮影地、蔵書、そしてフィルムという複数の痕跡を重ね合わせることで、写真の中には飯田という写真家の存在が間接的に立ち現れる。誰かの姿を直接撮るのではなく、その人物が見ていた風景や手にしていた本、残した素材を介して、その人の輪郭へと近づいていく試みだ。

1986年長野県生まれの篠田は、写真やヴィデオを主なメディウムとして、「記録」の実践とその再考をテーマに制作を続けてきた。消えつつあるものを記録する一方で、記録するという行為に不可避的に伴う恣意性や限界にも目を向け、その不完全さの先に生まれる可能性を探っている。

Hayley Atwell será Peggy Carter

Julio Vélez

Y con esta confirmación, Alice Eve queda descartada.

Marvel Studios anunció recientemente quién será la actriz que interprete a Margaret «Peggy» Carter, y no es otra que Hayley Atwell ( La duquesa , 2008). Recordemos que Peggy es el interés amoroso de Steve Rogers en el esperado filme Captain America: the First Avenger (2011). Esto, por supuesto, pone fin al rumor de la semana pasada que afirmaba que Alice Eve ( She’s Out of my League , 2010) sería la elegida para el rol.

Con esta noticia, resulta emocionante saber cómo desarrollarán, tanto Marvel como Atwell, a Peggy. Sobre todo, porque el personaje no es ninguna chica frágil, ya que en la historieta participó activamente con el Capitán en contra de los nazis.

Ahora que, sin importar quién de las dos actrices se hubiera llevado el papel, la elección intriga. Especialmente, porque el personaje a interpretar nació en el estado de Virgina, Estados Unidos, lo que nos dice que es una chica americana al cien por ciento. Esto es curioso porque, tanto Atwell como Eve, las principales opciones de actriz para Peggy Carter, son británicas.

¿Les gusta la pareja que hace con Chris Evans ? Veremos la química entre ambos actores durante el estreno en julio de 2011.

Julio Vélez Colaborador en web y revista Cine PREMIERE desde 2006. Me especializo en anime/manga, comics, doblaje, tecnología y videojuegos. Mis sagas favoritas: Doctor Who, Star Trek, Dragon Ball y Star Wars. Batimaníaco, geek ochentero y hardcore gamer.
